observations: Photo shows a PlayStation-style controller (dualshock layout) on top of a black box/cardboard with printed text.
The controller appears to be a custom/colored variant (blue/teal with red accents).
No console (PS4) body is visible in the photo.
No visible game discs/cases are shown.
No visible model/serial label, ports, or FC26/modchip markings are visible.

claims.claim: Ps4 fat hacked with fc26 and 8 other games
claims.evidence: Only a controller on a box is visible; no PS4 fat console, no FC26/modchip evidence, and no games are shown.

risks.risk: The item in the photos may not be the PS4 console (could be only a controller or unrelated item).
risks.proof: A photo showing the actual PS4 FAT console body (front + back ports) with the same controller/box, plus a close-up of the console label/serial.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not having the PS4 console (worst case: controller-only value).

risks.risk: Hacked/modchip claim (FC26) may be false or not functioning.
risks.proof: Video booting the console showing the hacked menu/indicator (or system info) and a close-up photo of the modchip area/board inside (or a clear internal photo).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working/hack not confirmed (worst case: treat as standard console with no confirmed mod benefits).

risks.risk: Game count/availability may be overstated (8 games may not be included, or may not run).
risks.proof: Clear photos of all included game discs/cases (or a video showing the games list on the console and launching at least one).
risks.if_unproven: Price as fewer/unknown games and assume games may not run (worst case: no working games confirmed).

risks.risk: Console condition (overheating, loud fan, faulty HDMI/USB, broken disc drive) cannot be assessed from this photo.
risks.proof: Video showing the console powering on, HDMI display output, fan behavior, and (if disc drive exists) inserting a disc and playing for a few minutes.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing repair / not fully functional (worst case: not working).

proof_requests: Photo of the actual PS4 FAT console (front, back ports, and top/side) matching the listing.
Close-up of the console label/serial (for model verification) and a photo of the disc drive area.
Video boot showing the hacked/modchip behavior (FC26) or system info that supports the claim.
Photos of all included games (discs/cases) and a video launching at least one game successfully.
response.reason: The photo does not show a PS4 FAT console, FC26/modchip, or any games—so the seller’s claims can’t be verified remotely. Request proof photos/videos of the console and working games before pricing.
